about: The glass bottle filled, broken, and the lamp thrown (V-FILL, WATER-F, BOTTLE-FUNCTION, LANTERN): the Kitchen has nothing to fill the bottle from; at the Dam, by the reservoir, it fills where it is open and empty, and not where it is full or stoppered; thrown, it shatters and its water spills; the brass lantern thrown is smashed on the floor, and its light goes out for good: what is left is a broken lantern, which will not light.

expect.words: West of House
You are standing in an open field west of a white house, with a boarded front door.
There is a small mailbox here.
There's nothing to fill it with.
The bottle is closed.
Opened.
The water slips through your fingers.
Thank you very much. I was rather thirsty (from all this talking, probably).
The bottle is now full of water.
It is a clear glass bottle with a stopper, of the kind made to carry water on long walks.
The glass bottle contains:
A quantity of water
Closed.
The bottle is closed.
The bottle hits the far wall and shatters. The water spills to the floor and evaporates.
Dam
You are standing on the top of the Flood Control Dam #3, which was quite a tourist attraction in times far distant. There are paths to the north, south, and west, and a scramble down.
The sluice gates on the dam are closed. Behind the dam, there can be seen a wide reservoir. Water is pouring over the top of the now abandoned dam.
There is a control panel here, on which a large metal bolt is mounted. Directly above the bolt is a small green plastic bubble.
The lamp has smashed into the floor, and the light has gone out.

There is a broken lantern here.

It is what is left of the brass lantern: a dented frame, a twisted handle and a good deal of broken glass, none of it inclined to give light ever again. It was a perfectly good lamp until somebody threw it.
Taken.
You can't turn that on.
You are carrying:
A sword
A broken lantern
